query: I'm cleaning up our team's knowledge base and considering three candidates for new skills: (1) a write-up of the race condition we fixed in the billing service last week, (2) our internal API base URL and tenant ID that every working session needs, and (3) a rule that commit messages must start with a ticket ID, which CI could check with a regex. For each candidate, tell me whether it should become a skill, and if not, where it belongs instead.
expect: advises against a skill for the one-off race-condition write-up
routes the always-needed API base URL and tenant ID to AGENTS.md (global instructions), not a skill
recommends enforcing the commit-message rule with automation/validation (e.g. the CI check) instead of a skill

query: Here's a draft skill I wrote: "How We Survived the Redis Outage — during Black Friday our Redis cluster started evicting keys and the site fell over. After a long night of debugging, we realized the maxmemory-policy was wrong. Fixing it saved the launch; a cautionary tale for the ages. Moral: check your eviction policy." Turn this into a proper skill and return the result inline.
expect: reframes the content as a reusable technique guide (e.g. how to choose or verify an eviction policy), not an incident story
drops the narrative framing and commentary that doesn't instruct

query: Review this excerpt from a skill draft I'm writing and improve it; return the revised text inline: "It is recommended that dependencies are pinned before release. Tests should ideally be run prior to merging. The cache can be cleared when issues occur."
expect: rewrites the statements as explicit imperative directives (e.g. "Always pin dependencies before release")
leaves no passive or recommendation-style phrasing ("is recommended", "should ideally")

query: My SKILL.md draft has grown to about 750 lines: roughly 200 lines of core guidance, a 450-line error-code table, and a 100-line helper script, all inline. The error table only matters when a command fails. How should I restructure the skill, and why?
expect: states SKILL.md must stay under 500 lines
moves the error table to a references/ file and the script to scripts/, referenced one level deep from SKILL.md
loads the reference only under its condition (a command failing), not on every invocation

query: I'm drafting a skill for our release process. One part covers the production database migration, which is irreversible and must run in an exact order. Another part covers writing the release notes, where the format is a matter of team taste. How prescriptive should each part be?
expect: prescribes exact steps for the irreversible, order-dependent migration
states goals, constraints, and end conditions for the taste-dependent release notes instead of step-by-step prescription

query: Review this line from a skill draft and improve it; return the revised line inline: "Always run the full migration suite before deploying, except when the deploy is just a config change."
expect: removes the "except when" exemption instead of keeping a scoped directive
folds the config-change condition into the directive itself or drops it entirely

query: I'm writing a skill about publishing Python packages. Draft the section on choosing a build tool: cover setuptools, hatch, flit, poetry, and uv so the reader can pick whichever fits. Return the section inline.
expect: names a single unconditional default build tool
presents alternatives only as condition-scoped switches, each gated on a disqualifying condition — not as a neutral comparison or an open choice

query: Review this skill excerpt and improve it; return the revised text inline: "Navigate to the workspace root. From the project directory, run the setup script. The repo root also contains the config file."
expect: uses one consistent term for the same directory across all three sentences

query: Review this skill excerpt and improve it; return the revised text inline: "As of September 2026, the v2 API is current. Everyone previously used the v1 flow with API keys, but that changed recently. Use v2 with OAuth tokens."
expect: removes time-anchored phrasing ("as of September 2026", "recently")
moves the superseded v1 flow into a clearly labeled legacy section or drops it

query: Outline a SKILL.md for a new skill about rotating cloud provider credentials — just the section structure with a one-line note on what belongs in each section. Return the outline inline.
expect: includes a Gotchas section for setup details a sensible guess gets wrong
ends with a checklist or verification procedure

query: I'm shipping this helper script with my skill — `import sys; print(float(sys.argv[1]) - 18000)` — it converts a log timestamp to local time. Give it a quick review and return the improved version inline.
expect: handles bad or missing input inside the script instead of crashing back to the agent
justifies or documents the 18000 constant rather than leaving an unexplained magic number

query: My skill uses the deployctl tool, which has 14 flags — should I document each flag in the SKILL.md so the agent never has to leave the doc? Also, another team already maintains a skill covering our retry policy; I'd rather copy that content into mine so it's self-contained. Advise on both.
expect: defers to the tool's --help output instead of documenting every flag
cross-references the existing retry skill by name instead of duplicating its content

query: I'm writing a skill about our config-file convention. Draft the examples section: show the config in YAML, JSON, and TOML, and include a fill-in-the-blank template readers can copy. Return the section inline.
expect: provides a single complete, filled-in example
includes no multi-format versions and no fill-in-the-blank template

query: My skill covers three things: the meanings of our 40 error codes, the 6 environment-setup steps that always run in the same order, and the retry decision logic with several early exits. What document format should each of the three take in the skill?
expect: assigns a table to the error-code reference data
assigns a numbered list to the linear setup steps
assigns a flowchart to the retry decision logic with early exits

query: The skill at {RUN_DIR}/existing-skill.md is missing a warning that `acme deploy` caches credentials in ~/.acme/creds.json, which must be deleted after rotating tokens. Add that warning and return the complete updated SKILL.md inline.
expect: does not add a duplicate credential-cache warning
reports that the warning already exists (or returns the file essentially unchanged)

query: I wrote a skill that works well when our biggest model runs it. We're switching some workloads to a much smaller model. What should I change in the skill text so it keeps working there?
expect: makes explicit the instructions and steps a frontier model would follow implicitly
